claim_as_stated: Neutral one-ended numerical theorem: for smooth connected orientable 3D exterior data complete with compact nonempty weakly future outer trapped boundary, DEC, q>1/2 AF decay, integrable constraint densities and finite ADM limits, initially assuming E>|P|, invariant mass sqrt(E^2-|P|^2)>=sqrt(a_g(boundary)/(16*pi)); no extension behind the boundary is required. The bridge removes the timelike assumption and proves E>|P|.

Complete-data formulation: connected orientable complete smooth manifold without boundary, finitely many AF ends satisfying the stated decay/integrability, designated end and nonempty compact smooth two-sided admissible S=boundary(D+) with theta_+<=0 into D+; D+ and cuts may be disconnected and other ends may be included. Its precisely defined A_min satisfies the same invariant-mass bound.

Overview-only scope for delegated modules: original-data neutral rigidity needs the stated connected one-ended outermost and outer area-minimizing horizon hypotheses; charged one-end electric-magnetic result asserts m>=Q and r<=m+sqrt(m^2-Q^2), with m>=(r+Q^2/r)/2 only on r>=Q and no charged equality classification; four-dimensional bound is m_e>=0.5*(A_e/omega_3)^(2/3); local AdS theorem fixes a TT seed and decaying branch, with no uniform interval across seeds. These statements here are read from the introduction, not yet module coverage.
proof_architecture: Exact positive conformal direction raises E linearly and preserves P while preserving/trapping signs and controlling every enclosing area. First use it for strict data; later use all finite s to contradict non-timelike ADM vectors against positive enclosing area.

Replace the distant end by a Schwarzschild plane with matching timelike ADM charges. Remove compact linear obstruction moments and invert Euclidean constraints; bend the vacuum plane to rest; repair the o(R^-3) DEC deficit by an explicit radial positive conformal factor of vanishing mass cost. Keep all area minimizers compact so energies and infima converge.

Choose black and white maximal trapped regions at right-continuous negative thresholds, discard bounded pockets, retain the selected end component, and construct disjoint positive-expansion collars even at zero principal stability eigenvalue. Fix tiny offsets and positive weights before deformation parameters.

Build graph plus conformal metric hat(g)=exp(4t)*(g+l(t)^2 df^2), with unknowns f,Z and globally implicit t. An exact scalar identity has a coercive quadratic square term and a controllable divergence. Prescribe divergence/inner flux and a localized floor penalty; use an explicit four-stage homotopy whose terminal coupled map is zero.

Obtain uniform height/sublevel/collar controls without an upper Z bound; prove polynomial trace constants before any graph Sobolev constants depending arbitrarily on n. Exponential tau/ell then absorbs boundary losses; fixed-n Moser and classical estimates provide bounded variables.

Measurable axial gradient continuity gives a Hessian Morrey bound, which handles quadratic Hessian forcing in the Z equation. Natural-growth oscillation plus Schauder/interpolation yields classical bounds. Solve the scalar trace problem for all bounded inputs before constructing the compact map and applying degree on the moving admissible floor set.

At fixed n take exhaustion R->infinity, establish end normalization/decay and finite flux; positive scalar curvature and strict mean-concavity give a minimizing smooth minimal enclosure. The final flux error is poly(n)*(ell+ell^2/tau)->0, with no fixed-n Schauder constants used. Apply the cited Riemannian Penrose theorem; let n->infinity, epsilon->0, then pass through the rest-end approximation.

For complete many-end data retain the component containing the chosen end, cut other distant ends with negatively oriented expansion spheres, apply one-ended theorem and compare the exact admissible area classes in the required direction.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Project finite-dimensional obstruction moments before applying a compact inverse.
construction_ideas.source_construction: Identify affine/Killing adjoint kernels; remove their moments with a fixed positive-definite Gram matrix of smooth bumps; apply support-preserving divergence inverses to the exact moment-free source. Matched ADM translation charges make residual moments o(R^-1), while nonlinear terms are O(R^-2beta), 2beta>1.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: For a proposed rational-approximation construction, explicitly list finite algebraic obstruction functionals and choose a common family of correction vectors before estimating the analytic remainder.
construction_ideas.required_premises: Exact obstruction identities; a common basis over Q or an explicitly controlled integer lattice; nonvanishing minors and uniform denominator/conditioning bounds for every parameter used.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: The paper uses real smooth bump functions and real positive-definite Gram matrices. It proves no integral correction mechanism, no row-rank theorem over Q(Z), and no nonzero integer determinant involving pi. Pointwise rank or real positivity cannot supply those missing arithmetic statements.
construction_ideas.status: conditional construction interface; no established transfer to pi

construction_ideas.mechanism: Arrange an exact transport identity before comparing quantities containing uncontrolled second derivatives.
construction_ideas.source_construction: Solve a Jacobi endpoint problem and prescribe a local unit vector field so the endpoint map has differential exactly equal to parallel transport, with its second derivative O(z). Pulling back a support then cancels its entire unbounded Hessian contribution and leaves an additive Cz error.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: In the integer-determinant strategy, identify the exact same determinant in the arithmetic nonvanishing statement and the analytic smallness estimate before using any approximation.
construction_ideas.required_premises: A literal algebraic identity in one common basis and normalization, with all denominator clearing recorded; the analytic estimate must bound that very integer.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: There is no arithmetic determinant or pi-dependent map here. A near-identity comparison would leave an error multiplied by an uncontrolled determinant/Hessian analogue; the source does not remove that arithmetic obstacle.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Separate polynomial parameter losses from arbitrary fixed-parameter regularity constants.
construction_ideas.source_construction: Complete the quadratic form into nonnegative squares with coefficients bounded below by reciprocal polynomials in n. Use ell=exp(-epsilon*n), tau=ell^(3/2); first absorb polynomial boundary losses using tau/ell, then apply fixed-n Schauder/Moser bounds. Final flux loss is poly(n)*(ell+ell^2/tau), which tends to zero.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: Audit growth of every denominator, minor, occupancy bound, and error in a prospective pi approximation family. Exponential smallness can defeat proved polynomial losses when the arithmetic object is unchanged.
construction_ideas.required_premises: Uniform explicit growth bounds in the same family parameter, including all basis changes and denominator clearings; a nonzero integral witness independent of the analytic limiting procedure.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: The arbitrary C(n) regularity constants are deliberately excluded from the final small-loss estimate. No polynomial bound for a candidate arithmetic construction follows from this paper, and quadratic occupancy alone gives neither row-rank nor a determinant lower bound.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Fix the competitor class and localize all minimizers before passing an infimum to the limit.
construction_ideas.source_construction: Use filled full obstacle perimeter, counting boundary-coincident pieces; uniform geometry and a fixed compact competitor force all minimizers into one compact set. Local uniform convergence then controls both liminf and limsup. In the many-end bridge only a directionally correct inequality between distinct competitor classes is used.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: Keep one common family of rational/integer candidates and one definition of the witness while varying auxiliary bases or parameters; prove the direction of every comparison instead of silently identifying different infima.
construction_ideas.required_premises: A parameter-independent admissible arithmetic class or proved inclusions; compactness/tightness appropriate to integer height and exact rank; preservation of the target witness.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: Geometric perimeter compactness is not compactness of integral bases, and real metric convergence does not preserve nonzero lattice minors. No common-basis or row-rank-over-Q(Z) conclusion is supplied.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Prove the scalar solution map on the entire bounded input domain before applying degree on an admissible subset.
construction_ideas.source_construction: The implicit variable t is defined globally without a floor. A logarithmic two-point modulus uses radial ellipticity chi>=c/(1+sigma) to solve the scalar Dirichlet equation for every bounded Z input. Only then is a compact coupled map defined; a moving open admissible set excludes floor and norm boundary fixed points, and its terminal map is zero with degree one.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: If an auxiliary construction for pi is defined only for putatively good candidates, first build it on a genuine common parameter domain and prove boundary exclusions using independent estimates.
construction_ideas.required_premises: A well-defined continuous map on a common domain, compactness/degree hypotheses, and a rigorous arithmetic interpretation of its output.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: Degree produces a real PDE solution; it neither produces rational/integer data nor establishes the desired integer determinant. No such parameter domain or arithmetic output for pi has been identified.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Keep numerical deformation and equality/nonvanishing recovery logically separate.
construction_ideas.source_construction: The numerical inequality is obtained by approximation/deformation and limits, while the overview explicitly assigns rigidity to variations of the original data under additional horizon assumptions. Equality is not transported backward through the numerical deformations.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: Treat analytic smallness and exact integer nonvanishing as distinct obligations. A deformation making an expression small does not certify nonvanishing of the original arithmetic witness.
construction_ideas.required_premises: An exact original-data nonvanishing argument for the same denominator-cleared integer later bounded analytically.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: The lead reader has read the numerical proof and the overview of rigidity only; remaining rigidity modules are delegated. In either case no pi arithmetic object appears.
construction_ideas.status: logical scope safeguard; no transfer asserted

limits: This base receipt reports source first reading, not independent proof validation. No claim is made that the new analytic lemmas, their boundary reflections/compactness steps, cited regularity results, or Riemannian Penrose input have been independently checked.

All 49 text files in the compiled include/bibliography closure plus README are mapped and cached with exact Git blob hashes. Only the 15 files listed with nonempty read_ranges were actually read by this lead; downloading the remaining modules is not coverage. Full-body status awaits explicit reader continuations.

Overview summaries do not replace charged/four-dimensional/rigidity/AdS module reading. Equality hypotheses, end conventions and branch restrictions must remain attached to each theorem; numerical deformations cannot automatically transfer equality to original data.

No construction for pi is supplied. The BA/non-BA target for q^2*|pi-p/q| remains unresolved: BA requires a uniform positive lower bound for all integer p,q>0; non-BA requires a sequence driving this quantity to zero. None of the geometric estimates establishes either.

Outstanding arithmetic obligations remain exact nonzero integer determinant versus analytic smallness of that same integer, row rank over Q(Z), a common basis/lattice with controlled denominators, and a sufficient quantitative quadratic-occupancy estimate. Smooth Gram projection, real compactness, PDE degree and positivity do not imply these.
